name: Gearbox
text: Add Runway Gen-4 to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It stabilizes lighting and motion in raw footage better than any other tool—critical for clean inputs before any AI processing. The trade-off is cost: Gen-4’s API is expensive per minute, but the quality jump justifies it. Skip this step and downstream tools waste compute on shaky, noisy frames.

name: Torque
text: The real risk isn’t Runway Gen-4’s cost—it’s that forcing a 1080p pipeline through it locks EXCAVA into a fixed resolution ceiling. A better alternative is testing Runway’s 4K upscaler first on a 10% sample of raw footage; if the lighting/motion stabilization holds at 4K, we gain headroom for downstream AI without the Gen-4 API tax. Settle it by running a 5-minute 4K test clip through both pipelines and measuring the downstream EXCAVA accuracy delta.

name: Gearbox

Add Runway Gen-4’s 4K upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. The trade-off is compute cost: 4K upscaling doubles processing time, but the extra resolution justifies it by reducing artifacts in final analysis. Skip this step and we cap EXCAVA’s potential at 1080p, wasting headroom in modern models.

name: Torque
text: The real risk isn’t compute cost—it’s that Runway’s 4K upscaler introduces artifacts that downstream AI mistakes for real detail, degrading EXCAVA’s output. Test instead with a 10% sample of raw 1080p footage run through both Gen-4’s 4K upscaler *and* a separate 4K AI upscaler (e.g., Topaz Video AI) to compare artifact profiles; if Topaz’s output preserves EXCAVA’s downstream quality better, drop Runway’s upscaler entirely.
